paragraphs.text: # no-sleep
English | 中文

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that keeps the computer awake while the Harness is
running, so a long agen

t task is not cut off by the screen turning off or the
machine going to sleep. One preference row ap
pears in **Settings → General**.

| Switch | Turn wake-holding on or off (persisted per profile) |
| Keep awake | *Screen and system*

or *System only* (screen off, work continues) |
| Status | Live state read from the Host: holding /
starting / off / error, plus the helper process id |
## How it works

The hold is one `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED
[| ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED])

` request, made from a dedicated thread inside a small
helper process that the Host half starts with

Windows PowerShell's `Add-Type`.
Windows keeps the request for as long as that thread is alive and

drops it with
the process, so:

- **quitting the Harness** releases the request immediately (the helper is a
child of the Host and e

ed in the settings row and restarted by the
Host's 30-second supervisor.

The helper is a separate process because a Host plugin only receives Harness
APIs — no Electron or p

rocess-level native bridge — and the Desktop ships no
native Node addon. A child process is the nati

ve surface a Host plugin does
have. It is spawned hidden, so no console window flashes.

Windows exposes no reliable user-mode query for "is a wake request currently
applied" (`powercfg /re

quests` requires elevation and runs in another session),
so the row reports what the Host can verify

: the helper is alive with the
requested flags.

| `GET` | `/no-sleep/api` | — | status JSON |

e"?: "display"\|"system" }` | saves, applies, returns status |

## Reference: the in-process helper

`native/` holds a .NET helper (`no-sleep.cs`, built by `native/build.ps1`) that
makes the same reque

st from a thread inside the Host itself. It works when a
Host can load an assembly into its own runt

ime, and it is the version to switch
to if a future release exposes that surface to plugins — the cu

rrent Desktop
Host loads plugin rows inside its cordis runner and does not. The plugin does
not use

it today; `native/build.ps1` is kept because it also documents what the
hold looks like at the Win32
